headline: CANADA INVESTMENT SUMMIT UNLOCKS C$500B — 63 MINING PROJECTS HEADLINE CARNEY'S TRILLION-DOLLAR PITCH TO GLOBAL CAPITAL
source_name: Office of the Prime Minister of Canada
snippet: Canada's first-ever Investment Summit on September 15 generated nearly C$500 billion in new investment commitments across 167 projects — with 63 specifically in the mining and critical minerals sector — anchored by BMO committing C$70 billion and TD committing C$150 billion in project financing over the next five years. Prime Minister Carney framed the summit as a structural shift in how Canada courts international capital, with the mining commitments spanning gold, copper, lithium, and rare earths projects from the Ring of Fire to the Northwest Territories, representing the largest single-day capital mobilization event in Canadian mining history.

headline: GLADIATOR DRILLS 21.2M AT 3.07% COPPER AND 1.19 G/T GOLD AT CUB EAST — YUKON PORPHYRY STRIKE CONFIRMED AT 350M, FIVE RIGS DEPLOYING Q4
snippet: Gladiator Metals Corp (TSXV: GLAD) reported September 15 step-out drilling results at the Cub East target within the Whitehorse Copper Project in Yukon — hole BCG-045 returned 21.2 metres averaging 3.07% copper, 1.19 g/t gold, and 24.65 g/t silver, while step-out BCG-050 delivered 47.0 metres at 1.01% copper, expanding the confirmed Black Cub trend to a minimum 350-metre strike within an interpreted 1.5-kilometre mineralized corridor. With 50,000 metres planned in a five-rig Q4 program and the zone open in all directions, the company is positioning Cub East as a potential bulk-tonnage copper-gold discovery in the Whitehorse Copper Belt.

headline: GEMDALE HITS 110M AT 1.18 G/T IN PHASE 1 FINAL HOLES — 14.01 G/T HIGH-GRADE INTERCEPT ANCHORS PONTIO'S 4KM OPEN STRIKE IN FINLAND
snippet: Gemdale Gold Corp (TSXV: GEMG) reported September 15 the final assay results from Phase 1 drilling at its Pontio Gold Project in Finland — the highlight hole PONT093 returned 110 metres averaging 1.18 g/t gold including a 5.19-metre interval grading 14.01 g/t gold, while two additional holes delivered 60.85 metres at 0.80 g/t Au and 47.16 metres at 0.82 g/t Au. The Phase 1 program has now traced bulk-tonnage gold mineralization over a minimum 4-kilometre strike that remains open at depth and along trend; a maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate is targeted for Q1 2027 with Phase 2 drilling to follow.

headline: ONGOLD RESOURCES FILES 2.0MOZ GOLD MRE AT MONUMENT BAY — 74MT AT 0.84 G/T INDICATED IN MANITOBA WITH TUNGSTEN CREDITS UNMODELLED
snippet: ONGold Resources (TSXV: ONAU) filed September 14 an NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate for its Monument Bay Gold-Tungsten Project in northern Manitoba — totalling 74.39 million tonnes grading 0.84 g/t gold for 2.003 million ounces, with approximately 80% classified in the Indicated category per SRK Consulting. The company notes that tungsten credits have not yet been incorporated into the resource model and that the primary gold system remains open at depth, with ongoing work targeting both resource expansion and the potential upside from co-product tungsten in a market where Western supply is increasingly constrained by China's export controls.

headline: PPX MINING HITS 8.66 G/T GOLD AND 290 G/T SILVER OVER 3.6M AT CALLANQUITAS — FIRST 2026 UNDERGROUND DRILL PROGRAM EXTENDS PERU VEIN TO DEPTH
snippet: PPX Mining Corp (CVE: PPX) reported September 15 the first results from its 2026 underground diamond drilling program at the Callanquitas vein system within the Igor Project in northwestern Peru — best hole CA-26-33 returned 3.60 metres averaging 8.66 g/t gold and 289.6 g/t silver including peak intercepts of 20.04 g/t Au over 0.85 metres and 2,251 g/t Ag with 3.0% Cu over 0.90 metres. Additional holes extend the Tension vein to the north, south, and at depth, confirming structural controls the company believes could host multiple parallel high-grade corridors requiring systematic follow-up drilling.

headline: PUREPOINT AND ISOENERGY CONFIRM 1.65% U3O8 AT NOVA — DORADO JV TRACES 1KM URANIUM CORRIDOR AT ATHABASCA UNCONFORMITY
snippet: Purepoint Uranium Group (TSXV: PTU) reported September 2026 winter assay results from the Nova Target at its 50/50 Dorado Joint Venture with IsoEnergy — highlight hole NV26-05 returned 1.65% U3O8 over 0.3 metres at 390 metres depth at the unconformity, with uranium mineralized intervals confirmed in multiple holes across an approximately one-kilometre corridor. The Nova Discovery was first confirmed in 2025 with grades up to 8.1% U3O8; the 2026 summer drill program has been completed with additional assay results anticipated in Q4, advancing one of the more active new discoveries in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin.

headline: INDONESIA'S NICKEL QUOTA CUTS BACKFIRE NEAR $16,570/T — CRUX INVESTOR: PHILIPPINE ORE FLOODS IN AS SMELTERS SIT IDLE
snippet: Crux Investor analysis examines why Indonesia's decision to cut its 2026 RKAB nickel mining quota 30-34% to 260-270 million tonnes — from 379 million tonnes approved in 2025 — is failing to lift prices above $17,000 per tonne: from January through July 2026, Indonesia imported 11.4 million tonnes of Philippine ore against 6.82 million a year earlier, effectively replacing withheld domestic feedstock while smelters process foreign ore and domestic miners sit idle. The piece frames the quota mechanism as increasingly undermined by Philippines import substitution and questions whether Indonesia can maintain sufficient supply discipline to reprice the market.

headline: KITCO'S COLUMBO: GOLD HOLDS PATH TO $5,000 WITH NEUTRAL POST-HIKE GUIDANCE — FED DECISION REMOVES THE PRIMARY HEADWIND
snippet: Kitco contributor Jesse Columbo's September 15 pre-FOMC analysis mapped two forward scenarios for gold: a 25-basis-point hike with neutral language yields a mild relief rally back toward recent highs; a hold on rates would have unleashed a run at $5,000. With the Fed delivering a hike to 4.00% alongside guidance traders read as neutral — not committing to a November follow-up — Columbo's bullish scenario is now fully active: the primary near-term headwind for gold has cleared, gold rallied $83 to $4,389 on the decision, and the $5,000 target sits back on the table for late 2026 if macro data cooperates.

headline: SPROTT MONEY: SEPTEMBER TO REMEMBER — GOLD AND SILVER OUTLOOK AFTER THE FED'S FIRST HIKE SINCE 2023
snippet: Sprott Money's post-FOMC September 16 analysis frames the Fed's 25-basis-point hike to 4.00% as a pivotal clearing event for precious metals — the first rate increase since 2023 was the most anticipated hike in recent memory, and with gold rallying $83 to $4,389 on the decision, the 'buy the news' pattern documented in every prior well-anticipated tightening cycle has reasserted itself. The piece outlines the path for both metals through year-end, noting that Goldman Sachs' $4,900 and JPMorgan's $4,500 gold targets remain intact while the silver structural deficit of 46.3 million ounces provides support regardless of near-term rate noise.

headline: 63 MINING PROJECTS IN CANADA'S INVESTMENT SUMMIT PROSPECTUS — RING OF FIRE, SHAAKICHIUWAANAAN LITHIUM, NWT CRITICAL MINERALS IN C$1T PITCH
snippet: NAI 500's project-level breakdown of Canada's September 15 Investment Summit identifies 63 mining and critical minerals projects among the 167 total investment opportunities presented to global institutional capital — including Ontario's Ring of Fire chromite and nickel complex, the Shaakichiuwaanaan lithium district in Quebec, and Northwest Territories projects spanning cobalt, tungsten, and rare earths. The analysis examines how the summit prospectus was structured to attract sovereign wealth funds and strategic investors beyond traditional mining finance, positioning Canada's resource base as a supply-chain alternative in the context of China's rare earth and battery metal export controls.
